description: Compute gross, operating and net profit margins from revenue, cost of goods sold and operating expenses.

faqs.a: Gross margin = (revenue − COGS) ÷ revenue. Operating margin = (gross profit − operating expenses) ÷ revenue. Net margin uses net income here (no taxes modeled).
faqs.q: How are the three margins calculated?

faqs.a: COGS is the direct cost of what you sold (materials, direct labor). Operating expenses are overhead: rent, salaries, marketing, admin.
It varies by industry — 10% net is strong for retail, while software often exceeds 20%. Compare against your own industry's benchmarks.
faqs.q: What is a good net margin?
